body.estimand_functional: \(R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), where \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\) is the independently defined Airy value certified by the exact-target face-robust all-count diagonal; the independent allocation \(q^\dagger\) has the same second-order value.

sampling_model.design: The causal game permits every outcome-independent assignment law, including dependence across labeled units and zero allocation to an arm. The comparator assigns independently with \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\). The face-robust prior is selected independently of the design; exact unit-permutation reduction is lossless at every fixed allocation count.
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population of \(n\) labeled units with three binary potential outcomes; the exact response-count orbit retains all eight response types.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly one of three arm labels is assigned to each unit, and the observation is the assigned label together with its binary outcome.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap condition is imposed. For every proper allocation face, the common-shift tangent gives a target derivative-one direction whose revealed arm marginals have derivative zero. This removes the earlier scalar-prior boundary failure, but the uniform Bayes-risk lower expansion on those faces remains a theorem obligation.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no superpopulation nuisance estimation. The lower-prior coordinates are a longitudinal target coordinate, a transverse contrast-orthogonal coordinate, and an independent common shift. Their product score has exact directional information \(J_x(k)+10\{\beta^2+\gamma^2\}/\varepsilon^2\); the fixed-parameter diagonal waits until its threshold absorbs this transverse cost.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The unrestricted two-arm binary minimax risk equals \(n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\) and is attained by Bernoulli randomization with nonlinear shrinkage.
For the two-arm bounded-outcome game, independent assignment remains minimax when estimators are unrestricted.
Under permutation-invariant law classes and linear estimation schemes, complete randomization with Neyman allocation is minimax.
A first-order local asymptotic minimax bound applies across broad sequential experimental designs, including multiple treatments.
Pairwise-independent inclusion attains the sharp bounded-total minimax risk within the class of unbiased estimators.
Limits of experiments yield asymptotically optimal treatment rules under average and minimax risk criteria in smooth models.
Second-order minimax optimality can be characterized through positive solutions of a problem-specific Schrodinger equation.

body.tldr: For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), the fixed-independent Airy upper expansion and the resulting one-sided unrestricted deficit bound remain proved. The scalar corrected Airy prior is now retained only as a refuted legacy construction. Its replacement adds an independent common-shift coordinate \(\zeta\): exact inversion of \([v,d^\dagger,\mathbf1]\) proves that every proper allocation face has a target-changing direction invisible on its observed arms, and the resulting three-coordinate prior has exact positivity, score-information, orbit-reduction, and fixed-input ordered-algebraic certificates. The sharp unrestricted equality is still open because these finite identities do not yet yield a target-specific Bayes expansion uniform over all allocation counts with a computable tail.

project_justification.gap: The accepted parent proves the \(n^{-4/3}\) order, while the fixed-independent theorem identifies the Airy coefficient. The former scalar lower prior fails exactly on a zero-count face. The new common-shift repair passes the finite tangent kill test and gives an explicit rational score ledger, but the missing theorem is still the design-independent Bayes bridge for the random exact finite-population target, uniformly across local counts, positive-count exterior allocations, and every proper face, with all-future computable errors.
project_justification.niche: At \(c^\dagger\), the basis \([v,d^\dagger,\mathbf1]\) separates the target, transverse, and common-shift coordinates. The common shift is essential: it makes the target coordinate unrecoverable from any one-arm or two-arm marginal experiment without imposing overlap. The unresolved scientific question remains whether unrestricted dependent designs improve on \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\) at second order.
project_justification.fill: The verified contribution now includes the eight-type tangent measures, exact proper-face score identities, explicit formulas for \(H(q)\), \(\beta(q)\), and \(\gamma(q)\), the rational information bound \(J_{\max}(k,\varepsilon)\), a finite eight-type and six-cell remainder ledger, a fixed-parameter diagonal threshold, the genuine three-coordinate prior, lossless orbit Bayes reduction, and a terminating same-input evaluator. The root theorem continues to state, without laundering, the uniform Bayes expansion and computable tail still required for the sharp equality.

body.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) and Hull (2026) establish two-arm sharp results, not the three-active-arm all-design converse here. The accepted parent supplies the exact orbit game, first-order value, second-order order, and finite certificates. The present repair is finite and problem-specific: it adds a common-shift tangent that guards every proper allocation face, proves lossless orbit reduction, and gives a terminating face-robust evaluator. Hirano and Porter (2009) and Levit (1986) motivate limiting-decision and spectral methods, but no cited result supplies the missing target-specific uniform Bayes bridge. Bai (2023), Armstrong (2022), and Aronow and Lopatto (2026) impose different design or estimator restrictions. Hammer et al. (1996) remains only a prospective complete binary-endpoint regimen-trial motivation; no censored-outcome reanalysis is claimed.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The legacy scalar Airy tube is refuted on the allocation \((n,0,0)\) by the exact deficit lower bound \( (11/8)\int |x|w_k^\dagger(x)\,dx+(45/256)\varepsilon\). The common-shift repair removes that infinitesimal identifiability failure and has positivity budget \(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+4\varepsilon)\le1\). Its product-score calculation contains the explicit \(\varepsilon^{-2}\) cost, so shrinking the transverse widths must occur only after a fixed-parameter threshold. Still missing is a sharp posterior-risk identity for the random finite-population target and displayed monotone bounds for local, shell, and face regions. The existential fixed-design remainder constant cannot serve as computable evaluator data. The finite \(K=3,n=3\) label gap remains only a diagnostic.
body.honest_scope: The root bridge is confined to the fixed rational contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\). Unconditionally proved results are the fixed-independent Airy expansion, its one-sided implication for the unrestricted game, the exact response geometry, the face-robust tangent and proper-face score identities, the effective rational Airy records, the lossless orbit reduction, and same-input face-robust Bayes and primal certificates. The unrestricted sharp equality and cross-sample effective certificate remain conditional on the open all-count bridge. No growing-arm, uniform vanishing-weight, or arbitrary-real computability claim is made; equality versus strict second-order loss of the independent design remains unresolved.
body.interpretation: A prospective trialist may use the proved independent allocation \(q^\dagger\), its total Airy-feedback estimator, and finite exact certificate machinery. The new face-robust prior shows algebraically why omitting an arm does not defeat the lower-prior target direction: an unobserved common-shift combination prevents recovery from every proper face. This is not yet evidence that dependent designs lack a second-order advantage, because the uniform exact-target Bayes expansion and its computable tail remain open.
